text.p: On commodity markets on Friday night, copper prices eased back in after-market trade on the London Metal Exchange on one big sell order.
Gold prices bounced higher in New York trade after their slump earlier in the week.
Oil prices rose as colder weather in the United States triggered expectations of winter demand for heating oil.
Wheat prices firmed after Turkey announced new ergot fungus limits for imports, raising expectations of imminent imports of U.S. wheat.
The CRB index closed up 0.98 of a point at 239.72.
Copper prices on the London Metal Exchange, which rebounded above $2,000 per tonne on Thursday, held most of the gains through Friday to close in London at $2,007.
But it eased just below $2,000 in later inter-office activity on one big sell order in thin volume that prompted some liquidation of long speculative positions.

Copper ended in London at $1,985 a tonne, down $32 from Thursday's close. A burst of investment bank buying and shortcovering had pushed three months delivery London Metal Exchange (LME) copper higher towards the end of the week.

Aluminium also firmed from a week ago on tight supply for January and speculative interest but ended Friday afternoon easing with copper to around $1,450. On COMEX, copper ended 1.2 cents down at 94.35 cents a pound despite a larger-than-expected drop in LME stocks Friday and news of a strike at a Chilean mine.
Nickel moved higher on the back of trade and merchant demand. It was last at $7,260, up $30.
Zinc dipped in thin trading and ended $4 lower at $1,064, while lead pressured by light long liquidation settled at $735, versus $749.
Gold and silver prices ended mostly higher in New York on Friday, as the complex continued to recover from a slump earlier in the week with help from the December gold and silver options expiry.
COMEX December gold closed up 90 cents at $380.50, after again finding support around $378 early in the day.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $379.20/379.70 an ounce, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $378.15, and the New York close Thursday at $378.75/379.25.
NYMEX heating oil and crude prices ended with steep gains Friday on short covering as a cold spell forecasted for the northeastern United States is expected to jump-start heating oil demand.
December heating oil ended 2.04 cents higher at 68.93 cents a gallon. December crude settled up 85 cents at $23.59 a barrel and rose as high as $23.70.
Temperatures were forecasted to be 10 to 14 degrees below normal this weekend until the middle of next week in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.
Traders said the rally in crude sharpened when buy programs were triggered after the price went above $23.00.
Traders also said crude prices received some support by a possible strike by oil workers of the state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela over privatization and benefit issues.
Earlier IPE crude futures closed 77 cents higher at $22.98 in London on the NYMEX rise.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on commercial buying with prospects for a resumption soon of wheat sales to Turkey cited, traders said.

A senior government agriculture official Friday said Turkey will set new ergot fungus limits for imported wheat that generally meet with U.S. export requirements. Talk continued to circulate that Turkey next week will be in the market for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of wheat.
Support also came from firm French wheat prices. Wheat closed one to 7-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with December up 3-3/4 at $3.78-3/4.
